scope: Reviewed low-strength 0x10 haptic frames over USB, overlapped 8 ms grid; no configuration/initialization/feature command
pattern: left 400 ms -> right 400 ms -> both 400 ms -> neutral tail

observation.segments_distinguished: three segments felt and mapped to left / right / both
observation.quality_note: user reported the felt quality differs from expectation; exact axis of difference not yet stated

compare_run.pattern: left 600 ms, right 600 ms, left 600 ms, right 600 ms, neutral tail

observation_compare.source: user report after compare run; corrected by the user to left
observation_compare.note: The LEFT side is reported duller/weaker, and the same side was not identical across its two appearances. Same packets, same 8 ms schedule, all writes accepted, so the variation is downstream of the transport.

compare_repeat.observation: second run: the left segment was again duller than the right in both appearances
compare_repeat.conclusion: left-grip dullness is reproducible across two runs and is treated as a device characteristic, not a transport or scheduling fault

findings: On an 8 ms grid with the write overlapped, dispatch lateness stays under 0.6 ms and all 162 frames reach the endpoint: the host path is end-to-end functional.
The reviewed low-strength packet produces a felt, side-separable output, so 0x10 output is honoured in Switch mode over USB.
Perceived quality is not characterised yet: the difference may be segment asymmetry, or a difference from native console haptics, or from the earlier Pico path.
limits: Perception is a single user report, no repeat, no blind comparison.
Only one amplitude/frequency pair was sent (LOW_160); the amplitude-to-feel mapping is unknown.
WriteFile completion is not controller ACK; the report proves timing and acceptance, not waveform fidelity.
next: Pin down what 'different' means (between segments, versus native console, versus the Pico path), then run a small amplitude ladder if the difference is strength.
